description: Every barrel (index.ts/index.mjs, or a non-index file whose content is >80% export-from statements) in this repository that has reached >= 6 `export * from` re-exports MUST have a row here - enforced by the `barrel-fanout-inventory` Architect check. Declaring is DESCRIPTIVE, never a judgment: a wide `export *` barrel is not automatically wrong, and a row here neither endorses nor condemns the fan-out - it makes the blast radius (import-graph coupling, editor/type-inference cost, chunk-bloat risk on a side-effectful re-export) visible on purpose instead of something only a hand grep would find. The gate fires ONLY on an UNDECLARED high-fan-out barrel; a declared one always passes, however wide. Seeded 2026-09-16 from the check's own repo-wide scan against this root (extensions .ts/.mjs): the single member below was the only barrel at or above the threshold, and the scan reported no other undeclared barrel.

members.reason: The orchestration layer's published surface: 13 `export * from` statements, one per focused module under `src/service/` (core, watch, actions, fetch-all, job, repo-mgmt, scan, reads, files, tree, conflicts, editors, guards). The fan-out IS what the layer is - the HTTP route modules, the fs watcher, auto-commit, remote-sync, the MCP tools and the CLI each import exactly one specifier (`./service/index.ts`) instead of reaching into 13 modules and privately re-deriving their ordering; the file's own header names every module's job so that surface stays readable. Everything that touches a repo goes through the per-repo operation queue those modules share, which is precisely why callers must not be handed the pieces. Consolidation candidate for a future named-re-export pass, the same treatment `no-passthrough-barrel` applied to the type hubs - but that is a repointing exercise across every route module, not something this inventory forces. Declared 2026-09-16; the declaration is descriptive, not an endorsement of the shape.
